problem:
The domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=(1-\operatorname{cot}⁡t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j+{t}^{2}\,k$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne .
$$

What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $1-\operatorname{cot}⁡t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ , $t\ne n\pi ,$ where $n$ is an integer.

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{sin}⁡2t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component ${t}^{2}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne n\pi ,
$$

where $n$ is an integer.
